ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Best-of-N distillation with an analytic divergence bound for text-to-image diffusion
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune Stable Diffusion 1.5 on its own best-of-N samples scored by ImageReward, using 1,500 training prompts from a LAION aesthetics caption pool. The best-of-N law has a known divergence from the reference, log N minus (N-1)/N, so the marginal KL is set by choosing N instead of being estimated along denoising trajectories. Train with the standard denoising loss on the selected images for 2 rounds, regenerating candidates from the updated model between rounds. Evaluate ImageReward, CLIP score and FID against COCO on 500 held-out prompts, and diversity as mean LPIPS across 4 samples per prompt.
CONTROLS: Reference model on the same prompts; DDPO with a trajectory KL penalty at 3 coefficients; RAFT-style top-1 filtering; sweep of N over 2, 4, 8 and 16; 3 seeds with bootstrap intervals; the measured divergence from an importance-weighted estimate compared with the analytic bound.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: Reward rises roughly with log N while FID stays within 2 points of the reference up to N=8, and the measured divergence tracks the bound. It could fail if the reward model is exploited by image artifacts, which held-out reward models would reveal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reward-tilted rejection fine-tuning of Stable Diffusion XL with four scorers
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune Stable Diffusion XL on filtered samples, keeping the top 1 of 32 candidates for each of 6,000 Pick-a-Pic prompts, scored by ImageReward, PickScore, HPSv2 and an aesthetic predictor. Run 5 rounds of regenerate-and-retrain at 1024-pixel resolution with 50-step sampling, training a separate copy per scorer. Estimate the marginal KL of each copy by importance-weighted sampling over 2,000 trajectories per checkpoint, and measure FID against COCO plus score gains on 5,000 held-out prompts at each checkpoint, with a CLIP-based diversity statistic over 8 samples per prompt.
CONTROLS: Base model sampled on the same prompts; one DDPO run per scorer with a trajectory KL term; top-1 of 8 filtering; cross-scorer evaluation matrix, where each copy is judged by the other three scorers; 5 seeds with bootstrap intervals per scorer; ablation over the number of candidates.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: Gains on the training scorer are large and transfer partly to the other three, with FID drifting upward after round 3. It could fail if the four scorers are so correlated that the cross-scorer matrix carries little information.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learned initial-noise tilt for memoryless flow fine-tuning of Stable Diffusion 3
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune Stable Diffusion 3 Medium toward a GenEval-based reward with a stochastic control objective whose optimum is the reference law tilted by the exponentiated reward. Convert the flow ODE into a memoryless noise-schedule sampler so that the terminal law is independent of the initial noise, and learn a separate tilt for the initial-noise distribution to remove the initial value bias. Train on 4,000 compositional prompts in batches of 8 trajectories with a one-step-denoised reward estimate for credit assignment. Report GenEval accuracy, FID on COCO, and CLIP score on a 1,000-prompt held-out split.
CONTROLS: Trajectory-KL PPO; the same control objective with the initial-noise tilt frozen at the standard Gaussian; reward-weighted regression; the unmodified model; 3 seeds; a sweep of the KL strength over 4 values; a held-out reward model (ImageReward) to detect over-optimisation.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: The learned tilt should beat the frozen Gaussian by a few GenEval points at equal FID. It could fail if the memoryless sampler itself lowers image quality enough to cancel the gain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Stochastic control fine-tuning of flow models over three scales and four rewards
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune three flow models (Stable Diffusion 3 Medium, a 1B-parameter class-conditional ImageNet flow, and a small CIFAR-10 flow) with a tilted-law control objective, converting each sampler to a memoryless noise schedule. Optimise four rewards in turn: GenEval accuracy, ImageReward, PickScore and a compressibility score, using 8,000 prompts for the text-conditioned model. Learn the initial-noise tilt for each combination, and repeat training with 5 seeds. Report accuracy, FID on COCO, ImageNet-64 and CIFAR-10, and CLIP score on 1,000 held-out prompts, with learning curves logged at regular checkpoints.
CONTROLS: Trajectory-KL PPO for each reward; the same objective with the tilt frozen; reward-weighted regression; the unmodified models; a sweep of the KL strength over several values; held-out scorers for each trained reward.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: The tilt helps most on the text-conditioned model and little on CIFAR-10. It could fail if the compressibility reward behaves unlike the perceptual rewards, so that conclusions do not carry across the four.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Stability of KL-regularised, KL-free and trajectory-KL reward fine-tuning at large scale
PROPOSAL: Compare three ways of fine-tuning Stable Diffusion XL on PickScore: policy gradient with trajectory KL, policy gradient with no KL term, and a tilt-targeting method that regularises the marginal law through best-of-N selection. Use 10,000 Pick-a-Pic training prompts and monitor, at fixed intervals, reward, FID against COCO, CLIP score, and the largest gradient norm. Define instability as reward collapse or FID above twice the reference value, and record the step where it first occurs. Run 3 seeds per method and 3 learning rates, using 4 inner updates per batch of 8 trajectories, and add a human-preference study of 300 prompt pairs.
CONTROLS: Unmodified model; each method at matched numbers of reward evaluations; KL strengths of 3 values for the regularised variants; held-out ImageReward as an over-optimisation check; seed-level bootstrap intervals; the human study with 3 raters per pair.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The KL-free run destabilises first, the trajectory-KL run is stable but plateaus at lower reward, and the tilt-targeting run reaches the highest reward at stable FID. It could fail if instability is driven mostly by learning rate rather than the regulariser.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reward fine-tuning stability across five model variants and many regularisation strengths
PROPOSAL: Compare trajectory-KL policy gradient, KL-free policy gradient and best-of-N selection on five diffusion models: Stable Diffusion 1.5, 2.1, XL, 3 Medium and a latent consistency variant. Use 12,000 prompts per model, scored by PickScore, and monitor reward, FID against COCO, CLIP score and gradient norm at regular checkpoints. Define instability as reward collapse or FID above twice the reference value. Run 5 seeds for each combination and 5 KL strengths, then correlate the collapse step with model size, and add a human-preference study over prompt pairs.
CONTROLS: Unmodified models; matched numbers of reward evaluations; learning-rate grid of 4 values; held-out ImageReward and HPSv2 as over-optimisation checks; bootstrap intervals; several raters per pair in the human study.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Collapse arrives earlier for larger models and weaker regularisation, with the best-of-N runs the steadiest. It could fail if collapse step is dominated by seed noise so that the correlation with size cannot be resolved.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Layout generation on PubLayNet with overlap and alignment rewards
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a discrete layout diffusion model pre-trained on PubLayNet toward a reward that penalises box overlap and misalignment, using rejection sampling on 5,000 generated layouts per round for 2 rounds. Regularise toward the reference with the best-of-N relation instead of a trajectory term, picking N=4. Evaluate overlap, alignment, FID computed in a layout feature space, and maximum IoU against the training set to detect memorisation, using 2,000 generated layouts per model. Train on one dataset and one model size so that the question of regularisation is isolated from scale.
CONTROLS: Reference model; trajectory-KL PPO; no-KL PPO; filtering with N=2 and N=8; 3 seeds; validation layouts as a ceiling on realism; a check that conditional constraints on category counts are preserved.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Overlap falls by about half with FID within 10 percent of the reference. It could fail if the reward is gamed by trivially small boxes, which the category-count check would expose.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Layout generation on three datasets with composite rewards and larger models
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune discrete layout diffusion models pre-trained on PubLayNet, RICO and Magazine toward composite rewards that combine overlap, alignment, aspect ratio and reading order, using rejection sampling on 40,000 generated layouts per round for 6 rounds. Use the best-of-N relation with N=16 and train each dataset at two model widths. Evaluate overlap, alignment, FID in layout feature space and maximum IoU against the training set on 10,000 generated layouts per model, with a user preference study over 200 layout pairs.
CONTROLS: Reference models; trajectory-KL PPO; no-KL PPO; filtering with N=4 and N=32; 5 seeds; validation layouts as a ceiling; per-reward ablations that drop one component at a time; category-count preservation check.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Composite rewards improve all three datasets, with the larger width giving small additional gains. It could fail if the four reward components conflict so that no setting improves them jointly.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Marginal-law regularisation for reward fine-tuning of an equivariant molecule flow model
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune an E(3)-equivariant flow matching model pre-trained on GEOM-Drugs toward a docking-score reward computed with AutoDock Vina against 2 protein targets, using the tilted-law control objective with a learned initial-noise tilt. Sample 20,000 candidate molecules per round for 3 rounds and keep the top fraction by docking score as training data, with selection size chosen to bound the divergence from the reference. Report mean docking score, validity, uniqueness, novelty, atom and molecule stability, and the Frechet distance between fingerprints of generated and reference molecules.
CONTROLS: Pre-trained model; trajectory-KL PPO; no-KL policy gradient; filtering at 3 selection sizes; 3 seeds; a check that top molecules are not near-copies of training molecules by Tanimoto similarity; a second docking engine on a subset as a held-out scorer.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Docking scores improve by about 1 kcal/mol at stable validity above 90 percent. It could fail if the reward is exploited through large, strained molecules that a second docking engine scores poorly.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reward fine-tuning of molecule flow models across datasets, targets and many rounds
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune E(3)-equivariant flow matching models pre-trained on QM9 and GEOM-Drugs toward docking-score rewards computed with AutoDock Vina against 8 protein targets, using the tilted-law control objective with a learned initial-noise tilt. Sample 100,000 candidate molecules per round for 8 rounds and keep the top fraction as training data, with a separate model for each target. Report mean docking score, validity, uniqueness, novelty, atom and molecule stability, and the Frechet distance between fingerprints of generated and reference molecules at each round.
CONTROLS: Pre-trained models; trajectory-KL PPO; no-KL policy gradient; filtering at 5 selection sizes; 5 seeds per target; Tanimoto similarity check against training molecules; a second docking engine on a subset as a held-out scorer; a transfer test across targets.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Gains saturate after round 4 and transfer weakly between targets. It could fail if docking noise across targets is large enough to obscure differences between methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Data-only correction of a pre-trained flow model through late-time velocity refinement
PROPOSAL: Take a pre-trained ImageNet-64 flow model sampled by a 10-step ODE solver and refine its velocity field on data samples alone, with a flow-matching loss that up-weights times close to the data end, where discretisation error concentrates. Train for 20,000 steps on the original training images with a small learning rate and no reward. Evaluate FID and precision-recall on 50,000 generated samples, and compare against simply raising the solver steps from 10 to 20 to see whether the refined model gives equal quality at half the sampling compute.
CONTROLS: Unmodified model at 10 and 20 solver steps; fine-tuning with the uniform time weighting; fine-tuning with a lower-rank adapter; 3 seeds; a held-out set of real images to check that FID gains are not memorisation; nearest-neighbour retrieval for duplicates.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: FID improves by 10 to 20 percent at 10 steps and approaches the 20-step baseline. It could fail if the gain comes from the loss weighting alone, which the uniform-weight control would show.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Data-only correction of flow models through repeated refinement over several solvers
PROPOSAL: Take pre-trained flow models on CIFAR-10, ImageNet-64 and ImageNet-256, each sampled with 5 solver configurations from 4 to 50 steps, and refine each velocity field on data alone with a flow-matching loss that up-weights times near the data end. Train each for 100,000 steps from 3 initialisations of the adapter. Evaluate FID, precision-recall and recall-weighted density on 50,000 generated samples per model and configuration, and compare against raising the solver steps, measuring generation compute at each setting.
CONTROLS: Unmodified models at each solver configuration; uniform time weighting; full fine-tuning against adapters at 3 ranks; 5 seeds; held-out real images; nearest-neighbour duplicate retrieval; a comparison with a distillation baseline.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: Refinement helps most at the smallest step counts and fades beyond 20 steps. It could fail if gains on CIFAR-10 do not appear at 256 pixels, where the error is dominated by the model rather than the solver.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exact marginal KL on CIFAR-10 flow fine-tuning to compare regularisation choices
PROPOSAL: Use a CIFAR-10 flow model whose likelihood can be computed exactly through the probability-flow ODE with a divergence trace estimator, so the marginal KL of a fine-tuned model is measurable. Fine-tune toward a brightness-and-contrast reward with trajectory-KL policy gradient, no-KL policy gradient, and rejection sampling with N=8 on 50,000 generated images. Record reward against exact marginal KL on 10,000 test images and ask which regulariser buys the most reward per unit of true divergence, and whether the trajectory KL overstates the true divergence.
CONTROLS: Reference model; 4 KL strengths per method; 3 seeds; a check of the trace estimator against an exact Jacobian on a small subset; held-out classifier accuracy to confirm samples stay realistic.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The trajectory KL upper-bounds the true divergence by a factor that grows over training, and rejection sampling attains the best reward per unit of true KL. It could fail if the trace estimator variance is large enough to blur the comparison.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Marginal KL tracking on flow fine-tuning with likelihood estimates for several datasets
PROPOSAL: Use flow models for CIFAR-10, SVHN, CelebA-64 and ImageNet-32, whose likelihoods are computed through the probability-flow ODE with a Hutchinson trace estimator using several probes. Fine-tune each toward brightness, sharpness and compressibility rewards with trajectory-KL policy gradient, no-KL policy gradient and rejection sampling with N=16 on 100,000 generated images. Record reward against marginal KL on 20,000 test images and fit curves for each combination, then relate the gap between trajectory and marginal KL to the training step.
CONTROLS: Reference models; 6 KL strengths per method; 5 seeds; trace estimator checked against an exact Jacobian on subsets of each dataset; held-out classifier accuracy; comparison of several ODE tolerances.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The gap between trajectory and marginal KL grows with training in every dataset. It could fail if likelihood estimates at 64 pixels are too noisy to separate the methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Initial value bias in a two-dimensional mixture and MNIST under trajectory KL
PROPOSAL: Build a toy study of the initial value bias: train a diffusion model on a two-dimensional 8-component Gaussian mixture and on MNIST, then fine-tune toward a reward that favours a single component or digit class. With trajectory-KL policy gradient, using batches of 64 trajectories for 500 updates, measure how far the initial-noise distribution drifts compared with the exact optimal tilt, which is computable on the mixture. Compare against a variant that learns the tilt of the initial noise explicitly. Report the total variation to the exact tilted target on the mixture and classifier-measured class proportions on MNIST, using 10,000 samples.
CONTROLS: Pre-trained model; no-KL policy gradient; rejection sampling; exact tilted density as the reference on the mixture; 5 seeds; sweep of KL strength over 4 values.
COST: 40
PREDICTION: Trajectory KL leaves a total variation near 0.15 while the explicit tilt reaches near 0.03. It could fail if the toy mixture is so simple that the bias is invisible in MNIST.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Initial value bias across mixtures, MNIST, CIFAR-10 and a latent image model
PROPOSAL: Extend the study of the initial value bias: train diffusion models on mixtures with 4, 8 and 16 components in two dimensions, plus MNIST, CIFAR-10 and a latent Stable Diffusion model, and fine-tune each toward reward functions favouring a single component or class. With trajectory-KL policy gradient, measure how far the initial-noise distribution drifts from the exact optimal tilt, and compare with a variant learning the initial tilt explicitly. Report total variation on the mixtures and classifier class proportions elsewhere with 50,000 samples per run.
CONTROLS: Pre-trained models; no-KL policy gradient; rejection sampling; exact tilted densities on the mixtures; many seeds; sweep of KL strength over many values; a check over several noise schedules.
COST: 40
PREDICTION: The bias grows with the number of components and the explicit tilt removes most of it. It could fail if class proportions on CIFAR-10 move for reasons unrelated to the initial noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Intermediate-state reward estimates for credit assignment in diffusion fine-tuning
PROPOSAL: Exploit the multi-step structure of sampling by scoring noisy intermediate states with the reward of their one-step denoised prediction, and use these scores as per-step advantages in fine-tuning Stable Diffusion 1.5 toward the LAION aesthetic predictor. Train on 3,000 prompts with batches of 4 trajectories per prompt. Compare the final-sample reward used for all steps against the intermediate estimates, and measure aesthetic score, CLIP score and FID against COCO, plus the correlation between the denoised-prediction reward and the final reward at 5 noise levels.
CONTROLS: Final-reward policy gradient with trajectory KL; reward-weighted regression; best-of-4 selection; 3 seeds; ablation of the noise levels at which intermediate estimates are used; a shuffled-advantage control.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: Intermediate estimates reach a given aesthetic score in about half the reward evaluations. It could fail if the correlation at high noise levels is too low, making early-step advantages noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Intermediate-state rewards, lookahead rollouts and value networks for credit assignment
PROPOSAL: Score noisy intermediate states by the reward of their one-step denoised prediction, by short ODE lookahead rollouts and by a learned value network, and use the three as per-step advantages when fine-tuning Stable Diffusion 1.5, 2.1 and XL toward the LAION aesthetic predictor, PickScore and ImageReward. Train on 10,000 prompts with batches of 8 trajectories per prompt. Measure each reward, CLIP score and FID against COCO, along with the correlation between each estimate and the final reward at several noise levels.
CONTROLS: Final-reward policy gradient with trajectory KL; reward-weighted regression; best-of-8 selection; 5 seeds; ablation of the noise levels used for each estimator; a shuffled-advantage control; a value network of two sizes.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: Lookahead rollouts give the best credit assignment per sample but the one-step estimate is cheapest per unit of reward gain. It could fail if estimator quality differs between rewards, so no single ranking holds.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Policy gradient against best-of-N distillation at matched sample budgets on Stable Diffusion XL
PROPOSAL: Test how policy-gradient fine-tuning with a KL penalty relates to best-of-N distillation for diffusion models. Fine-tune Stable Diffusion XL on PickScore with each method at 4 matched reward-evaluation budgets, using 8,000 Pick-a-Pic prompts, and plot reward against estimated marginal KL, using importance sampling over 1,000 trajectories. Fit the policy-gradient frontier and compare with the log N minus (N-1)/N divergence of best-of-N selection to test whether selection traces the same reward-divergence frontier.
CONTROLS: Unmodified model; policy gradient with trajectory KL at 5 strengths; best-of-N with N from 2 to 32; Reinforce-Rej with threshold filtering; 3 seeds; held-out ImageReward and HPSv2; FID against COCO.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Both families trace similar frontiers once evaluation budgets match, with selection slightly ahead at low divergence. It could fail if the importance estimator is too noisy to place the frontiers within their intervals.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Policy gradient against best-of-N distillation across scales, rewards and sample budgets
PROPOSAL: Compare policy-gradient fine-tuning with a KL penalty against best-of-N distillation on Stable Diffusion 1.5, XL and 3 Medium, with PickScore, ImageReward, HPSv2 and an aesthetic predictor, at 8 matched reward-evaluation budgets. Use 20,000 Pick-a-Pic prompts and plot reward against estimated marginal KL from importance sampling over 4,000 trajectories per checkpoint. Fit frontiers per model and reward, and compare them with the divergence of best-of-N selection to see how scale shifts the match.
CONTROLS: Unmodified models; trajectory-KL policy gradient at 7 strengths; best-of-N with N from 2 to 64; Reinforce-Rej with threshold filtering; 5 seeds; held-out scorers; FID against COCO; a comparison of learning rates.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Frontiers agree within noise for small models and diverge for larger ones. It could fail if differences between rewards dominate any effect of scale.
